**issue (bug_risk):** Unexpected errors are re-raised instead of returning a JSON 500 response, which is inconsistent with other endpoints.

In `list_public_posts`, unexpected exceptions are logged and then re-raised, whereas `get_public_post` logs and returns a JSON `{"error": "An error occurred"}` with a 500 status. Re-raising here will likely produce a generic HTML 500 instead of JSON, breaking consistency for clients of the public posts API. Please return a JSON 500 response here as well to align error semantics with `get_public_post`.

**suggestion:** The `listPublicPosts` API call isn’t typed, so the response is effectively `any`.

Other API calls use generics on `apiClient.get` (e.g. `get<PublicPostResponse>`) so the response is type-checked. Here, `apiClient.get('/posts/public', ...)` has no generic, so `response.data` isn’t validated against the expected `{ posts, total_count, total_pages, page, limit }` shape. Please define a `ListPublicPostsResponse` type and call `apiClient.get<ListPublicPostsResponse>(...)` to restore type safety.
